content.body:
The Panzer III was originally intended to be the main battle tank for the panzer divisions, but development difficulties saw it pass through four models before the F version was finally accepted and put into production.
A solid medium tank design, its gun was nevertheless slightly underpowered in coping with the Allied tanks. The chassis and frame were later upgraded again and again, seeing service throughout the war on all fronts.
Control Variations: none ... operates as per the manual.
The Panzer IIIF is the typical German tank, an archetype whose characteristics are representative generally of the early German panzers against their opponents: fast, reliable, with outstanding optics enabling precise fire from long ranges, and good suspensions making it easy to fire while moving.
Relatively thin armor compared to French tanks, slightly weaker guns, the Pz.IIIf is still a good tank when handled competently: do not try to engage any but light AFV from the front ... use your superior vision and mobility to keep on the flanks, and be patient enough to hold fire until you have a good shot. Your commander is only useful if he is able to see ... leave him unbuttoned most of the time (pull him in during air attack or if you are entering an urban area) if he is killed, the slight risk to your tank (through his open hatch which will then remain open) will have been more than offset by his utility to that point if you use him a lot to spot for you.
Move quickly from cover to cover, use shadows and brush to break up your outline as much as possible.
